Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. FinOptics is moving our pilot of the private VPC deployment into a formal security audit next week (PCI scope). Before the audit we need a short architecture readout from Redwood covering control-plane / data-plane separation, telemetry controls, and evidence we can hand to our security team.

Concrete asks from FinOptics:
- A single-page control/data separation diagram that shows management/control plane endpoints, data-plane egress paths, and tenant demarcation.
- A short list of telemetry artifacts you can provide (logs, traces, retention windows, sampling guidance).
- Confirmation of where KV cache resides and whether it is accessible from tenant workloads.
- Proof of egress proofing for PCI (how egress is constrained and how failover is handled).
- A small bundle of artifacts we can upload to our compliance portal (diagram PDF, short runbook, and a signed statement of retention/rotation policy).

We attached our rough sketch to help orient the conversation (finoptics-vpc-sketch.pdf). Ideally we can get the Redwood deliverables by Monday so our audit lead has time to review. Can you confirm owners and ETA?

Respectfully,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, FinOptics Inc.

Hi Alicia — thanks for the sketch and the clear list. Kimberley and I reviewed with the infra and observability teams this morning. High level plan and owners below; attaching a short audit plan we will use as the basis for the artifact bundle.

What Redwood will provide (summary):
- Control/Data separation diagram (PDF + source diagram) — owner: jonas_weber — ETA: Mon 22 Jun EOD. This will mark control-plane endpoints (API, admin UI), data-plane endpoints (node IP ranges), and tenant demarcation lines.
- Observability & retention summary (markdown) — owner: kimberly_park — ETA: Mon 22 Jun noon. Contains what logs/traces are collected, retention policy, and sampling rates (token-level traces are possible with consented capture; see note below).
- KV cache statement (signed) — owner: marissa_cole — ETA: Mon 22 Jun EOD. Will state whether KV cache is tenant-local or co-located and how it is scoped for private deployments.
- Egress proofing outline + failover behavior — owner: karthik_iyer — ETA: Mon 22 Jun EOD. Will include routing constraints, allowed egress endpoints, and fallback policy to alternate region or model variants.
- Evidence pack (zipped) aimed at compliance portal: diagram PDF, runbook excerpt, signed retention statement — will be uploaded to the Drive folder and sent to you.

Notes / constraints:
- For PCI scope, we recommend enabling per-tenant egress allowlists and turning on KV cache isolation (both available for Dedicated/Private); if you need us to flip these before audit, please confirm TODAY.
- Token-level traces: we can enable higher-fidelity traces but this is opt-in and has storage/retention considerations (we’ll call out the trade-offs in the observability doc).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-audit-plan.md (this includes the action items and the template of the signed statements).

Action items:

- Redwood owners: produce artifacts and post to the Drive link we shared.

Best,

Alicia — final deliverables are attached and uploaded to the Drive folder. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

On Sat, 20 Jun 2026 at 11:20 -0700, Alicia Gomez <agomez@finoptics.com> wrote:
> Packet-level SLAs: they want a short statement on expected packet loss and latency impact during failover (is there a published SLA or expected performance envelope?).

We do not publish a per-packet SLA for Private deployments, but we provide operational targets and proven envelope for the dedicated GPU pools. Short statement included in the evidence pack: expected median p99 latency add-on during regional failover is ~60–120ms depending on model and sequence length; packet loss is controlled to <0.1% in normal failover paths. This language is in redwood-evidence-pack.zip (evidence/egress-sla.txt).

> Egress allowlist enforcement: can you provide example iptables/ACL rules (or a sample ACL export) we can show our network team?

See sample ACL snippet (evidence/acl-sample.txt) in the zip. It includes CIDR examples and required control-plane API endpoints. For your environment we recommend applying the ACL at the border gateway and at the cluster egress proxy (we called this out in the diagram).

> Per-tenant token traces: we'll opt-in for higher-fidelity capture for the audit window, but we need to know retention and export format so our compliance tooling can ingest.

We can enable tenant-scoped trace capture for a configurable window (recommended 7 days for audit ingestion). Export is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with masked tokens unless you request raw captures and sign the capture consent form. The retention and export spec are in the observability runbook linked: https://docs.redwood.com/vpc-observability-runbook.

Artifacts uploaded: redwood-evidence-pack.zip (diagram PDF, signed retention statement, sample ACL, SLA text, runbook excerpt). Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFINOPTICS-VPC.

I also created a short ticket for follow-ups: INFRA-4321 (link below). If you confirm we should enable per-tenant egress allowlists now, we will schedule the configuration window (approx 2 hours maintenance) and communicate the exact time.

Links / tickets:

Thanks — will keep monitoring the ticket and stand ready to support the audit call.

Best regards,
